items.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024
items.q: whether it’s Duke Ellington or Louis Armstrong or the Delta blues guitar players or the country meets city blues that birthed this scene basically, it wasn’t written down necessarily.

ctx.x: have been his phrase, but it made me think about how can you justify at an institution like you’re in, one famous around the world, if you wanted to spend a lot of time teaching young jazz musicians to use their ear, can you justify that in a curriculum?

Absolutely. Jazz is an aural tradition first I think. I don’t think it was written down in the beginning, much like classical was probably not. Until the word “classical” was put on it was probably not written down. The refinement of our tools has pushed us into this western music corner of what to define as what to be taught. And in theoretical terms that’s a heavy discussion, but in basic terms to me this music, which is jazz, is an aural tradition much — whether it’s Duke Ellington or Louis Armstrong or the…
Can you spell aural for me?
